rounds.answer: Assuming independent lane indices and one atomic per lane, for 32 uniform picks across 1,048,576 bins, expected distinct keys are M[1−(1−1/M)^32], about 31.9995, so only about 0.0005 atomics per warp are theoretically redundant. For the skewed case, one hot bin has probability 0.9 and each of the other M−1 bins has probability 0.1/(M−1). Expected distinct keys are 1−0.1^32 +(M−1)[1−(1−0.1/(M−1))^32], about 4.05, so about 27.95 atomics could be eliminated by perfect same-warp aggregation. That does not imply similar byte savings: the index and value inputs are still read for every lane, and atomics may require read-modify-write traffic, cache-line ownership or serialization; aggregation reduces atomic operations, not necessarily the input bytes or proportional DRAM traffic.
